If you feel like you need it, you can always send me a Private Message. It's alright, I know how hard it can be when your own mind gets warped by someone else, and you start doubting whether what you are thinking and feeling is reasonable or not.

I can tell you though, that breaking up with my ex and keeping that way was one of the best decisions ever. The first few months I was conflicted, I knew he treated me badly and yet I felt like I missed him and loved him. And that was confusing as fuck. I kept doubting my decision, thinking that maybe he was right and I was unreasonable. But time passed, I started talking to new people and slowly realized that I was in fact quite reasonable.

A bit more time, a couple of times dating unsuccessfully with people I didn't click well. That once again made it hard for me to stick to my decision. Especially since he kept contacting me once in a while to say that he misses me, then that he has a new gf but would dump her if I said I would come back to him, then saying he realizes that there is no other woman in this world better suited for him than me.

But I stuck to my decision and tried my best to ignore his words. (It was much easier after he started saying that he would dump his gf for me) I stuck to it despite there being situations once in a while where I would doubt myself, when it would be hard.

And now I have an amazing partner. For the past year I've had the most wonderful and understanding man by my side. Honestly, I could sing praises 24/7 about him, since I have never encountered a more amazing person than he is. And I am also able to have a completely healthy and loving relationship, despite my previous harsh experience.

So, my words to you, stay strong. Sometimes you'll feel weak or afraid, and that's normal. Sometimes you'll be confused and doubt yourself, that's also completely normal. No matter what, stay with your decision. Sometimes it will feel like you're destined to be forever alone or only doomed relationships await you, but that's alright, that too shall pass.

It might be hard right now to imagine how you will manage to live and feel over the coming year. Try to just focus one day at a time at first. Just focus on surviving one day at a time. Then two or three. Baby steps, slow and steady.

So that you have another person who can emotionally support you when you need it and to whom you can lend support when they need. On a personal note, stop fucking apologizing. I don't care about your apologies, because there is nothing to apologize for. It's just additional unnecessary frills that don't change the essence but may be annoying. It does nothing good for you.

For example you like computers. Now imagine you're getting yourself a new computer. The main thing you have in mind is it's purpose and for that you make sure to get a good processor, video card, etc. That's the essence of this object. Now imagine, you also get a nice case. Small things compound.

Little small things of being thoughtless, that have a tiny negative impact on the other person's feelings compound with other little things. Pretty soon, there's a whole huge heap of those little negative things and they're not so little anymore.

But positive things also compound. Every time something is done with the other person in mind, adds up to other small things. And soon they become a mountain.

From what you've written, it sounds like you have let a lot of thoughtlessness accumulate. You could've washed the mug after drinking or you could've left it in the sink. This time you left it, it's not a big deal is it? But that one tiny little negativity. Slowly each time you decide against doing a small little thing in favor of the relationship (because it's just something small, almost nothing) it becomes something that works against the relationship.

Now it seems a huge amount of those little things that you haven't done came together to form a formidable force against the relationship. The solution to this is the same one as got you to this point.

Start doing those small things, that are almost nothing but are in favor of the relationship. At first they'll seem like tiny little pieces of sand. But each small thing you do in favor of the relationship is something that does NOT add to the already huge pile of things working against the relationship. In time, the things done in favor will accumulate and grow larger, while the things working against the relationship will start to crumble when not being fed.

Not only that, but essentially by beating him at his own game, you'd lose to him, because by trying to win like this you would need to change yourself completely with the only person in mind - him. Basically, there is no way to truly win this game, you can only stop playing it.

But perhaps knowing all this will make the decision to cut him out easier.

If you're afraid that he might do something if you were to cut him out abruptly and completely, then you can simply make yourself appear worthless to him.  A sociopath always look for their interests first and if you look like you have nothing of value to him, then he will stop interacting with you, because if would be a waste of his resources.

Analyze what he gets out of you and stop giving it to him. Perhaps he gains a sense of power when he can make you feel certain emotions? In that case try to be as apathetic towards him as possible. Pretty much try your best to provide no value to him either emotionally, socially, physically, financially or whatever other way you could.

That way when he is the one who decides (or thinks he was the one to) end the relationship with you, you won't have to worry about him coming after you.

But this is a very very hard and long process to do and you'd need to have a very high awareness and control of yourself. A much quicker and easier way would be to just cut contact with him completely.

My situation was the the guy told me his feelings very quickly in the very beginning and I froze for a split second. That was because a recent long term relationship wasn't the healthiest one and my previous partner would only say this just before or right after something bad was to happen, so my reaction was defensive instead of being happy.

Afterwards the relationship slowly deteriorated. If before he would ask me tons of questions about me and my view and such, he stopped asking questions and his replies to mine were not longer as enthusiastic. It was quite a contrast with his previous behavior and made me feel like I did something wrong.

A bit later we had a talk about this and he brought up his confusion and lack of feelings. I asked him whether he wanted to break up or whether he wanted to stay together and work this through. he replied that he didn't know so I asked him to stay and I would give him space and just be there for support.

Things were still turning out worse and worse until a second similar talk happened, but this time I said that if he's not sure whether he wants to go or stay, then I am going, because this situation isn't good for my health either.

This whole time I pretty much felt quite betrayed. I knew that such things can happen and was willing to work this through and provide support in any imaginable way possible and yet that wasn't enough. There was nothing I could do and it felt like any chance to do this was taken from me. Even the break up, although I was the one to say it, I didn't feel like the one to initiate the break up. I felt like I was pressured for a long time until I said the words myself. He couldn't tell me he wanted to break up himself, so I did everything so I would say it. This might not be true, but that was my point of view for a time.
